zh.principle: **标准**：SHA-3 派生函数：cSHAKE、KMAC、TupleHash 与 ParallelHash（SP 800-185）（SHA-3 Derived Functions: cSHAKE, KMAC, TupleHash and ParallelHash (SP 800-185)）。摘要首句给出文件性质与对象：「This Recommendation specifies four types of SHA-3-derived functions: cSHAKE, KMAC, TupleHash, and ParallelHash, each defined for a 128- and 256-bit security strength.」随后逐个自述：「cSHAKE is a customizable variant of the SHAKE function, as defined in Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 202.」、「KMAC (for KECCAK Message Authentication Code) is a variable-length message authentication code algorithm based on KECCAK; it can also be used as a pseudorandom function.」、「TupleHash is a variable-length hash function designed to hash tuples of input strings without trivial collisions.」与「ParallelHash is a variable-length hash function that can hash very long messages in parallel.」它规定的是四个函数族及其 128/256 两档强度，全部派生自 FIPS 202。摘要的口径止于此：它给出四个函数族、两档强度与每个族的自述，不给出任何协议里应取的值，也不定义 KECCAK 或 SHAKE 本身——FIPS 202 是它的上游，本文件只在派生函数这一层作规定。
zh.why: §1 交代缺口在域分离：「Domain separation ensures that different named functions (such as SHA3-512 and SHAKE128) will be unrelated.」再把定制化的作用讲清：「Customization is analogous to strong typing in a programming language; such customization makes it extremely unlikely that computing one function with two different customization strings will yield the same answer.」其余三族要补的是基本函数没有的能力：「It then defines three additional SHA-3-derived functions, in Secs.4 through 6, that provide new functionality not directly available from the more basic functions.」风险因此被写成同一件事的两面：没有域分离，不同用途的输出可能彼此相关；有了 N 与 S，两次计算可被当作互不相干的函数。
zh.used: 分工写在编号章节：函数名不归用户，§3.4 说 N「This is intended for use by NIST in defining SHA-3-derived functions, and should only be set to values defined by NIST」，并直接约束用户：「Users of cSHAKE should not make up their own names--that kind of customization is the purpose of the customization string S, to be discussed in Sec.3.5.」§3.5 把选择权交给调用方：「The cSHAKE function also includes an input string (S) to allow users to customize their use of the function.」四族一律提供 128 与 256 两档：「cSHAKE, KMAC, TupleHash, and ParallelHash are all defined for two claimed security strengths: 128 bits and 256 bits.」两处的层级都是建议级：N 只应取 NIST 定义的值（原文 should only be set），名称也不建议由用户自创（原文 should not make up their own names）；S 由调用方选取，§3.5 只给出示例并允许实现限制其长度，本文件不为任何用途指定定制串。
zh.broken: 限度有四处。一是参数无下限：「The customization string may be of any length less than 22040; however, implementations may restrict the length of S that they will accept.」（留存文本把 2 的 2040 次方抽成了 22040：同文件 right_encode 的有效性条件也印成同样丢掉上标的 0 x < 22040，可见上标在提取时丢失；此处照抄抽取件原样并如此说明）取值仍由协议或应用自己决定，本文件不指定用途。二是越界的代价：「Nonstandard values of N could cause interoperability problems with future NIST-defined functions.」三是 cSHAKE 自身的性质缺口：「Note that cSHAKE does not share this property.」「For q1< q2, cSHAKE(X, q1, N, S) is a prefix of cSHAKE(X, q2, N, S).」即短输出只是长输出的前缀，不像另外三族那样换长度即换函数。四是实现边界：「An implementation of cSHAKE may reasonably support only input strings and output lengths that are whole bytes; if so, a fractional-byte input string or a request for an output length that is not a multiple of 8 would result in an error.」另外，「Appendix B--Hashing into a Range (Informative)」标题自标为非规范性附录。
zh.history: 扉页首行为「NIST Special Publication 800-185」，作者与部门两行连读为「John Kelsey Shu-jen Chang Ray Perlner Computer Security Division Information Technology Laboratory」，DOI 行是「This publication is available free of charge from:」，DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-185。Authority 段的引用行给出日期与页数：「Natl.Inst.Stand.Technol.Spec.Publ.800-185, 32 pages (December 2016)」，同段限定适用面：「such standards and guidelines shall not apply to national security systems without the express approval of appropriate federal officials exercising policy authority over such systems」。关键词行整行列出：「authentication; cryptography; cSHAKE; customizable SHAKE function; hash function; information security; integrity; KECCAK; KMAC; message authentication code; parallel hashing; ParallelHash; PRF; pseudorandom function; SHA-3; SHAKE; tuple hashing; TupleHash.」。致谢页点名 KECCAK 团队的评审者：「The authors thank the KECCAK team members: Guido Bertoni, Joan Daemen」，另有一句「The authors also thank their colleagues for reviewing drafts of this document and contributing to its development.」以上各条合起来是这份文件的门板事实：出版物编号、三位作者与所在部门、免费获取的 DOI 行、带页数的正式引用行，以及致谢点名的外部评审者；文本未声明取代任何早期版本。

en.principle: **Standard**: SHA-3 Derived Functions: cSHAKE, KMAC, TupleHash and ParallelHash (SP 800-185) (SHA-3 派生函数：cSHAKE、KMAC、TupleHash 与 ParallelHash（SP 800-185）). The opening sentence of the abstract gives the character and the object: "This Recommendation specifies four types of SHA-3-derived functions: cSHAKE, KMAC, TupleHash, and ParallelHash, each defined for a 128- and 256-bit security strength." The four are then self-described one by one: "cSHAKE is a customizable variant of the SHAKE function, as defined in Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 202.", "KMAC (for KECCAK Message Authentication Code) is a variable-length message authentication code algorithm based on KECCAK; it can also be used as a pseudorandom function.", "TupleHash is a variable-length hash function designed to hash tuples of input strings without trivial collisions." and "ParallelHash is a variable-length hash function that can hash very long messages in parallel." What is specified is four function families in two strength tiers, all derived from FIPS 202. The abstract's range stops there: four families, two tiers, one self-description each, no value prescribed for any protocol, and no definition of KECCAK or SHAKE themselves, since FIPS 202 is the upstream standard and this file works at the layer of derived functions.
en.why: Section 1 states the gap as domain separation: "Domain separation ensures that different named functions (such as SHA3-512 and SHAKE128) will be unrelated." It then explains what customization buys: "Customization is analogous to strong typing in a programming language; such customization makes it extremely unlikely that computing one function with two different customization strings will yield the same answer." The other three families answer to a second gap: "It then defines three additional SHA-3-derived functions, in Secs. 4 through 6, that provide new functionality not directly available from the more basic functions." The risk is therefore one thing seen twice: without domain separation outputs for different purposes may be related, and with the name N and the customization string S two computations can be treated as unrelated functions.
en.used: The division of duties is stated in numbered sections. The function name is not the user's to invent: §3.4 says of N that "This is intended for use by NIST in defining SHA-3-derived functions, and should only be set to values defined by NIST", and addresses users directly: "Users of cSHAKE should not make up their own names--that kind of customization is the purpose of the customization string S, to be discussed in Sec. 3.5." Section 3.5 hands the choice of S to the caller: "The cSHAKE function also includes an input string (S) to allow users to customize their use of the function." Across that division the tiers are fixed: "cSHAKE, KMAC, TupleHash, and ParallelHash are all defined for two claimed security strengths: 128 bits and 256 bits." The two parameters therefore sit at different levels: N is NIST's to define and users are advised not to invent names, both in should-level wording, while S is the caller's to choose — §3.5 gives only examples and lets implementations restrict its length, and no customization string is prescribed here for any use.
en.broken: The limits are stated in four places. First, no parameter floor and no assigned use: "The customization string may be of any length less than 22040; however, implementations may restrict the length of S that they will accept." (the retained extraction drops the superscript: the bound prints as 22040 where the document gives 2 to the power 2040, and the same file renders right_encode’s validity condition ) — the values remain the caller's choice, and this Recommendation assigns none to a use. Second, the cost of overstepping: "Nonstandard values of N could cause interoperability problems with future NIST-defined functions." Third, a property cSHAKE lacks: "Note that cSHAKE does not share this property." and "For q1< q2, cSHAKE(X, q1, N, S) is a prefix of cSHAKE(X, q2, N, S)." — a short output is merely a prefix of a long one, unlike the other three families where changing the length changes the function. Fourth, the implementation boundary: "An implementation of cSHAKE may reasonably support only input strings and output lengths that are whole bytes; if so, a fractional-byte input string or a request for an output length that is not a multiple of 8 would result in an error." The functions are specified; how a protocol uses them is not, and one appendix marks itself non-normative: "Appendix B--Hashing into a Range (Informative)".
en.history: The first title-block line reads "NIST Special Publication 800-185", the author and division lines read in sequence as "John Kelsey Shu-jen Chang Ray Perlner Computer Security Division Information Technology Laboratory", and the free-access line reads "This publication is available free of charge from:" followed by the DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-185. The citation inside the Authority block carries the date and length: "Natl. Inst. Stand. Technol. Spec. Publ. 800-185, 32 pages (December 2016)", and the same block bounds application: "such standards and guidelines shall not apply to national security systems without the express approval of appropriate federal officials exercising policy authority over such systems". The keyword line reads "authentication; cryptography; cSHAKE; customizable SHAKE function; hash function". The acknowledgements name the reviewers from the KECCAK team: "The authors thank the KECCAK team members: Guido Bertoni, Joan Daemen" — the next name carries a diacritic in the retained text, quoted here outside the name — plus "The authors also thank their colleagues for reviewing drafts of this document and contributing to its development." Together these are the front-matter facts of this file: the publication number, the three authors and their division, the free-access DOI line, the citation carrying its page count, and the outside reviewers named in the acknowledgements; the text claims no supersession of an earlier edition.

zh: cSHAKE：SHAKE 的可定制版本，除输入与输出长度外还接受函数名 N 与定制串 S。
KMAC：基于 KECCAK 的可变长消息认证码，也可用作伪随机函数。
TupleHash：对输入串元组哈希、以避免平凡碰撞的可变长哈希函数。
ParallelHash：把超长消息分块并行哈希的可变长哈希函数。
security strength：本文件为每个函数声明的两档强度，128 比特与 256 比特。
customization string (S)：由用户选取、用来把同名计算彼此隔开的输入串。
en: cSHAKE: the customizable variant of SHAKE, taking a function name N and a customization string S.
KMAC: a variable-length message authentication code based on KECCAK, usable as a pseudorandom function.
TupleHash: a variable-length hash function that hashes tuples of input strings without trivial collisions.
ParallelHash: a variable-length hash function that hashes very long messages in parallel.
Security strength: the two tiers this file defines every function at, 128 and 256 bits.
Customization string (S): the user-selected input that separates computations of one function from another.
